item.title: Homes sales fell 8.4% in January despite lower mortgage rates
item.description: Sales of previously occupied U.S. homes fell sharply in January as higher home prices and possibly harsh winter weather kept many prospective homebuyers on the sidelines despite easing mortgage rates. Existing home sales sank 8.4% last month from December, to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 3.91 million units, the National Association of Realtors said Thursday. item.title: These popular air purifiers are being recalled over a fire risk
item.description: Airova is recalling 191,390 Aroeve air purifiers over concerns that they could “overheat and ignite, posing fire and burn hazards to consumers,” according to a recent notice from the Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC). Airova received 37 reports of the air purifiers overheating—including one incident that resulted in a fire—however, there have been no reports of injuries or property damage. item.title: Long-term mortgage rate dips back to just above 6%
item.description: The average long-term U.S. mortgage rate is holding at just above 6% after reversing a modest uptick in recent weeks, just as the housing market closes in on the spring homebuying season. The benchmark 30-year fixed rate mortgage rate slipped to 6.09%, from 6.11% last week, mortgage buyer Freddie Mac said Thursday. One year ago, the rate averaged 6.87%. item.title: More Americans than ever love being single. But they feel penalized for it by our financial system
item.description: Single this Valentine’s Day? You’re not alone. New research from The Harris Poll shows that nearly half of Americans (46%) are not in relationships—many of them on purpose. The report, shared exclusively with Fast Company, calls it a “cultural revolution,” in which people are using singlehood as a way to prioritize their agency rather than focusing on traditional relationship expectations. item.description: If you live near an AI data center, you may already be seeing higher electricity bills. item.title: The next great American innovation is in the trades
item.description: For decades, America has told a singular story about success, suggesting that the only acceptable path to success is a four-year degree. item.title: If AI is doing the work, leaders need to redesign jobs
item.description: Most managers are using AI the same way they use any productivity tool: to move faster. It summarizes meetings, drafts responses, and clears small tasks off the plate.
